research_page.title: MAPT Rx (BIIB080) in mild AD (Phase 1b)
research_page.description: A Phase 1b trial demonstrating that the tau-targeting antisense oligonucleotide MAPT Rx is well-tolerated and substantially reduces CSF tau levels.
research_page.authors_line_md: Catherine J. Mummery et al. — Ionis Pharmaceuticals and Biogen
research_page.takeaway_md: MAPT Rx (BIIB080) successfully engaged its target in a Phase 1b trial, reducing CSF total tau and p-tau181 by over 50% at higher doses in patients with mild Alzheimer's disease. The drug was generally well-tolerated, providing foundational proof-of-concept for tau-silencing therapies, though an exploratory signal of increased ventricular volume requires ongoing monitoring.
key_findings_md: Higher doses of MAPT Rx (60 mg monthly, 115 mg quarterly) reduced CSF total tau by more than 50% from baseline at 24 weeks post-treatment (paper, Abstract).
The drug was well-tolerated; 94% of treated patients reported adverse events compared to 75% on placebo, with all treated events being mild or moderate (paper, Table 2).
The most common adverse event was post-lumbar puncture headache, and no serious adverse events occurred in the treated group (paper, Primary endpoint of safety).
Treated groups exhibited a slightly greater mean increase in ventricular volume at 6 months (0.5-0.7%) compared to the placebo group (0.2%) (paper, Extended Data Table 2).
research_page.methods_md: Phase 1b randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multiple-ascending dose trial. Enrolled 46 adults aged 50-74 with mild Alzheimer's disease. Participants received intrathecal administrations of MAPT Rx or placebo over a 13-week treatment period, followed by a 23-week post-treatment monitoring phase ([NCT03186989](/trials/mapt-rx-nct03186989)).
research_page.trial_evidence_md: This Phase 1b study ([NCT03186989](/trials/mapt-rx-nct03186989)) provides the primary clinical proof-of-concept for target engagement via antisense-mediated tau suppression. A larger Phase 2 trial ([CELIA](/trials/diranersen-celia-nct05399888)) was launched to assess clinical cognitive efficacy, though 2026 reports indicate conflicting accounts on whether it met its primary cognitive endpoints.
research_page.sentiment_md: Public perception is largely optimistic, heavily driven by enthusiasm from scientists and biotech investors over the novel gene-silencing mechanism and robust biomarker data. However, media narratives frequently blur the lines between successful biomarker reductions and unproven clinical cognitive benefits, while patient community awareness remains notably low.
caveats_md: The trial was small (N=46), brief (13 weeks of active treatment), and enrolled an exclusively white population, significantly limiting generalizability.

Treated patients showed a slightly accelerated increase in ventricular volume relative to placebo, a potential sign of 'pseudoatrophy' or neurodegeneration that requires careful longitudinal tracking in larger cohorts.
relates_to_md: [Amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) — Represents a major non-amyloid, tau-centric approach to disease modification.
[Biomarkers](/research/biomarkers) — Heavily reliant on CSF tau and p-tau readouts to prove CNS target engagement.

trial_pages.title: IONIS-MAPTRx Phase 1b
trial_pages.description: Phase 1b multiple-ascending dose trial of MAPT Rx (BIIB080) in mild Alzheimer's disease.
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Number of Participants With Adverse Events That Are Related to Treatment
trial_pages.why_md: This early-stage trial answers whether an antisense oligonucleotide can safely engage its target and suppress tau production in the human central nervous system. It laid the foundation for advancing [tau-lowering therapies](/research/papers/maptrx-antisense-tau) into larger clinical efficacy studies.
status_log_md: **2023-04-24** — Results published in Nature Medicine, confirming safety and robust dose-dependent tau reduction.
trial_pages.results_md: The trial met its primary safety endpoint with mostly mild-to-moderate adverse events (primarily post-lumbar puncture headaches). It demonstrated strong proof-of-concept by reducing CSF total tau and p-tau181 by over 50% in the highest dose cohorts.

trial_pages.title: CELIA (Diranersen Phase 2)
trial_pages.description: Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating diranersen (BIIB080) in mild cognitive impairment or mild AD dementia.
trial_pages.population: Mild Cognitive Impairment or Mild AD Dementia (50-80 years)
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Dose response in Change From Baseline to Week 76 on the CDR-SB
trial_pages.why_md: Designed to answer whether the robust tau biomarker reductions achieved by diranersen in Phase 1 translate into a meaningful slowing of cognitive decline on the CDR-SB scale.
status_log_md: **2026-07-01** — Phase 2 data presented at AAIC; media reports indicate a miss on the primary cognitive endpoint despite continued target engagement.
trial_pages.results_md: As of mid-2026, media coverage from AAIC indicates the trial failed to meet its primary cognitive dose-response endpoint, though it successfully continued to demonstrate biomarker target engagement. Official registry updates are pending.

timeline_entries.title: 2023-04 — First evidence of tau reduction via ASO
timeline_entries.body_md: Results from a Phase 1b trial of MAPT Rx (BIIB080) demonstrate that an intrathecally administered antisense oligonucleotide can safely and robustly lower CSF tau levels in humans. See [MAPT Rx Phase 1b](/research/papers/maptrx-antisense-tau).

timeline_entries.title: 2026-07 — CELIA Phase 2 misses primary endpoint
timeline_entries.body_md: Diranersen (BIIB080) reportedly misses its primary cognitive endpoint (CDR-SB) in the Phase 2 [CELIA trial](/trials/diranersen-celia-nct05399888), though biomarker target engagement remains strong.

notes_for_editor: Major discrepancy found regarding the Phase 2 CELIA (NCT05399888) trial results. The clinical-trials researcher reported results as pending/null with a March 2026 completion date. Conversely, the sentiment researcher referenced July 2026 media coverage (likely from AAIC) indicating the trial missed its primary cognitive endpoint. I have constructed the CELIA trial page and timeline entry reflecting the likely July 2026 AAIC readout based on the sentiment data, but this requires final human confirmation before publishing.
